steps.description: Registered session 1 via start_session (github-copilot / anthropic / claude-opus-5 / high); preload read; transport profile is copilot-cli via the seat-local local-overrides.yaml, so no provider API keys are required or warned about.

Shipped ai_router/verify_type.py: resolve_verify_type() is the one entry point for all three branches (project file -> environment default awaiting one confirmation -> guided setup), with write_project_verify_type() as the confirm-once-and-remember step and a `python -m ai_router.verify_type` CLI (--confirm / --set / --json; exit 3 = guided setup required) for the terminal the agent is already in. The file wins silently over the environment (standing decision 5) and an invalid value in EITHER is reported, never guessed at -- a bad project file does not fall through to the environment.

config.load_config no longer defaults transport.profile independently: it calls verify_type.derive_transport_profile after the local-overrides merge, so the project file outranks the tracked config AND the seat-local override, and the api default is now the last step of resolution rather than a parallel answer. Falsifiers (L-112-1) plant the disagreement in BOTH directions and assert the file wins, plus two look-alikes proving the derivation does not fire indiscriminately, plus a structural bijection assertion against config._VALID_TRANSPORT_PROFILES. 16 tests, all green; the neighbouring config / local-overrides / entry-point suites stay green.

Audited the four named modules BEFORE writing detection code. config.py resolves and validates transport.profile (:504 default, :232 copilot-cli block); copilot_preflight.py owns seat readiness (binary / credential / live-probe); transport_diagnostics.py owns failed-dispatch diagnosis; orchestrator_identity.py owns the effective provider. Grep confirms NOTHING resolved a verify type anywhere: no project-verify-type, AI_ORCHESTRATION_VERIFY_TYPE or verify_type reference existed outside the design doc and this set's spec. Nothing was reimplemented: verify_type.py is stdlib-only (so config can import it without a cycle), adds the resolution ORDER the four never had, and delegates readiness to the existing preflight CLI by naming it in the guided-setup script rather than re-checking a seat itself.

Code frozen after the round-5 VERIFIED verdict, then the full suite ran once: 3952 passed, 9 skipped in 484s, recorded via run_of_record (digest 25178fd4cad8). Verification took five rounds -- two discovery, two remediation-review, and one the operator authorized past the bound -- ending VERIFIED with six fix verdicts accepted and no findings. Disposition authored, lessons cited (L-112-1, L-069-1, L-064-8), committed and pushed.

Step 3.5: appended Session 2 ai-assignment.md block (what the session actually was, the operator stop and its ruling, the one class every finding belonged to, why the pre-verification falsifiers missed it, the irony-budget overage, and next-orchestrator / next-set recommendations authored directly under the temporary verification-only policy window).

Shipped check_direct_api_precondition() and providers_with_keys() in ai_router/verification.py. It compares the providers whose api_key_env actually resolves against the EFFECTIVE provider from orchestrator_identity (resolved in route() via resolve_session_orchestrator_identity), never a configured seat label. It never raises and never blocks: an unresolvable input reports applies=False, which keeps the cross-provider exclusion, so the fail direction is always verify-normally. Scope is the project committed verify type == DIRECT_API only -- a Copilot seat keeps its fail-closed ProvenanceUnavailable contract and an UNCOMMITTED environment default cannot relax anything (Session 1s suggestion-vs-answer rule). route() warns on stderr and yields the orchestrator exclusion only on that one degraded path; the permission is derived inside route() rather than accepted as an argument, so I-084-S1-3 (a caller-supplied list that omits the orchestrator) stays closed.

classify_verification_qualification() is the single mechanism that decides whether a verdict is qualified; every writer calls it rather than comparing providers itself. The qualification travels on the three router-owned verdict records, omit-null: the stamped metrics row (complete_stamp, from the provider that actually answered), the sN-issues.json envelope (verificationQualification), and disposition.json (verification_qualification, actively REMOVED when a later unqualified round supersedes a qualified one). validate_stamped_row check 5 now enforces a bijection -- a same-provider row passes only if it declares the qualification, and a cross-provider row declaring it is refused -- so a weaker verdict can never be read as corroborated, nor the flag become decorative. disposition.py validates the closed vocabulary and fails closed on an unknown token. Deliberately NOT written to session-state.json: the design docs open question 2 reserved the Explorer surfacing call, and operator decision P4 locked no orchestrator info in the Explorer (journaled).

ai_router/tests/test_qualified_verdict.py: 9 test functions (12 collected cases), landing Sessions 1-2 exactly on the specs 25-function irony budget (S1 shipped 16). Both directions are PLANTED, not read: a declared same-provider row corroborates a close (VALID and CARRIES the flag); an undeclared same-provider row is refused (the Set 084 F2 guarantee intact); a CROSS-provider row wearing the flag is refused (the half a one-way check would miss -- without it the flag could be attached unconditionally and would distinguish nothing); an unknown token is refused (closed vocabulary). Scope guards plant the harshest input, no keys at all, against COPILOT_CLI / unresolved / a case-folded look-alike, and drive the route boundary itself: a project with no committed file but AI_ORCHESTRATION_VERIFY_TYPE=DIRECT_API must NOT relax the exclusion, or one exported variable would silently weaken every verdict on that machine. Verified by probe that the same boundary returns degraded=True once the file is committed. The ordinary cross-provider row is deliberately not re-tested -- every stamped fixture in five existing suites is one.

Verification took four rounds: discovery fan-out (4 Major), supplementary (1 Major), remediation-review cycle 1 (5 fix verdicts accepted, 1 new in-hunk Major), remediation-review cycle 2 VERIFIED with 6 fix verdicts accepted and no findings -- inside the enforced bounds (2 discovery passes, 2 remediation-review cycles), no operator authorization needed. Every finding was accepted; none disputed. The common shape was that the machinery was correct and UNREACHABLE: _init() died at config load before the precondition could run, verify_session re-imposed the exclusion route() had just lifted, the qualification was dropped between complete_stamp and the metrics row the close gate reads, the disposition JSON Schema (additionalProperties:false) rejected the field, and disabling a keyless provider left its MODELS selectable so a pinned keyless verifier still died at dispatch. The reachability falsifier caught a NameError (sys unimported in __init__.py) that would have crashed every degraded run -- found by driving the branch, not by reading it (L-112-1). Code frozen after the VERIFIED verdict, then full pytest ran once: 3967 passed, 9 skipped in 522s, recorded via run_of_record (digest b94dd9168bf5).
